newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils extend their understanding of fractions by reading fractional scales, comparing equivalent fractions, and working with fractions greater than one whole.

This lesson includes:
✔ Representing fractions accurately on number lines
✔ Reading horizontal, vertical and circular measurement scales
✔ Using fractional scales to measure length, volume, capacity and mass
✔ Identifying the value of each increment on a scale
✔ Recognising equivalent fractions such as two thirds and four sixths
✔ Comparing fractional measurements expressed with different denominators
✔ Solving practical problems involving rulers, measuring jugs and weighing scales
✔ Understanding how complementary fractions combine to make one whole
✔ Exploring fractions greater than one whole
✔ Writing improper fractions as mixed numbers
✔ Counting beyond one whole in quarters, thirds, sixths and other fractions
✔ Representing improper fractions and mixed numbers using models
✔ Representing fractions greater than one on number lines
✔ Locating fractions and mixed numbers between whole numbers
✔ Estimating the position of fractions on unmarked number lines
✔ Classifying fractions as less than, equal to or greater than one whole

Pupils begin by revisiting fractions on number lines before applying the same ideas to real measurement scales. They learn to identify equal increments and use them to read fractional lengths, capacities and masses.

The lesson then develops equivalence and comparison, including examples where fractions look different but represent the same quantity, and practical problems that require pupils to compare fractional measurements.

Later, pupils move beyond one whole. They explore improper fractions and mixed numbers using chocolate bars, squares and rectangles, then count in fractions across whole-number boundaries.

The final section applies these ideas to number lines. Pupils locate mixed numbers, interpret missing values, estimate fractional positions and sort fractions according to whether they are less than, equal to or greater than one whole.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to read fractional scales, recognise equivalent fractions, represent fractions greater than one whole as improper fractions and mixed numbers, and locate them accurately on number lines.
